findings.reason: The diff removes `range.replace(BUILDSTRIPRE, '')`, so range.js:115 now runs HYPHENRANGE on raw input. In internal/re.js:144-149, XRANGEPLAIN allows `src[t.BUILD]?` only inside the patch group, so a partial endpoint with `+build` cannot match HYPHENRANGE (re.js:209). The string is then split on spaces, the lone `-` reaches Comparator and throws, and the build strip in parseComparator at range.js:258 runs too late to help. The test fixtures only use full versions with build metadata (`1.2.3+asdf - 2.4.3+asdf`), so no locked test catches this and no AC-N is shown broken. I'm treating it as an unintended behaviour regression and keeping it at medium, not the high in X1, because it only affects an uncommon input form.
findings.claim: Removing the up-front BUILDSTRIPRE strip from parseRange breaks hyphen ranges whose partial endpoints carry build metadata (e.g. `1.2+build - 2.3+build`, `1.x+build - 2.x`): strict mode throws Invalid comparator, and loose mode silently produces a different range.
findings.evidence: The diff deletes `range = range.replace(BUILDSTRIPRE, '')` from parseRange, so the hyphen replace at line 115 (`range.replace(hr, hyphenReplace(...))`) now sees raw build metadata. In internal/re.js:144-149, XRANGEPLAIN only allows `src[t.BUILD]?` inside the innermost (patch) group, and HYPHENRANGE (re.js:209) is anchored `^\s*(XRANGEPLAIN)\s+-\s+(XRANGEPLAIN)\s*$`, so `1.x+build` cannot match it. The range is then split on spaces, and the lone `-` goes to parseComparator/Comparator. That throws in strict mode, and the COMPARATORLOOSE filter at line 143 drops it in loose mode. The per-comparator strip `comp.replace(re[t.BUILD], '')` at line 258 runs only after the hyphen step, so it does not help. The x-range fixtures in test/fixtures/range-parse.js:91-118 contain no hyphen-range cases with build metadata.
